author: alone99
text_post: Last night, I met a very attractive woman in a class I'm taking. She was pleasant and soft-spoken and seemed to have a good sense of humor. We didn't get to chat much, but I was clearly interested in learning more about her.  Well, today I learned all I needed to know. I looked on her Facebook page and discovered that she's engaged. When I read this, I was actually relieved. I used to be disappointed when a woman to whom I was attracted had a boyfriend or was married. But now it's the opposite. If I see a ring on a girl's finger, I know that I won't have to face the humiliation of being rejected if I were to ask her out. Or even worse, having her become another oneitis. I'm too old to be pacing the floor and wondering what my "next move" is going to be in order to impress a woman.  When I see people in relationships (and who are clearly having sex), it's like peering into another world. How did that relationship begin? Even if the guy is not a Chad, how did he convince his partner to go on that first date? The simple answer is, he asked her, dummy! True, but more often than not, women are going to say 'No' when approached. And even if she agrees to go out with him, that's no guarantee that it's going to blossom into anything more than a platonic relationship (if that).  The bridge from being an incel to having a loving partner is like trying to walk across the Grand Canyon on a tightrope while blindfolded. In my case, I've never gotten past the first couple of steps.  Meeting this woman last night was just another reminder of what I've missed out on all these years (58 and counting) and what I'll never have. The caress of a woman's body, her kisses, and ultimately intercourse, are experiences I can't imagine. I live with it every day, and I know nothing will change. But the desire is still there. I guess I wouldn't be human if it weren't.
